questions.question: What does ADDIE stand for?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans ADDIE stands for
  • A – Analysis
  • D – Design
  • D – Development
  • I – Implementation
  • E – Evaluation
  • It’s a widely used instructional design model that guides the process of creating effective training
  • and educational programs.

questions.question: How does application and skill practice benefit employees?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans:Application and skill practice help employees reinforce learning, build confidence, improve
  • performance, and effectively transfer knowledge to real work situations.
questions.final_answer: Ans:Application and skill practice help employees reinforce learning, build confidence, improve

questions.question: How does training help organizations retain employees?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Training boosts employee engagement, enhances skills, shows commitment to growth
  • increases job satisfaction, and reduces turnover by promoting career development.
questions.final_answer: Ans: Training boosts employee engagement, enhances skills, shows commitment to growth

questions.question: Name three training delivery methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Three training delivery methods are
  • Instructor-led training (ILT)
  • E-learning (online training)
  • On-the-job training (OJT)

questions.question: In what way does training foster innovation within an organization?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Training fosters innovation by encouraging creative thinking, updating skills, promoting
  • collaboration, and empowering employees to develop and implement new ideas.
questions.final_answer: Ans: Training fosters innovation by encouraging creative thinking, updating skills, promoting

questions.question: What are the four primary programs in the TWI model?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The four primary TWI programs are Job Instruction, Job Methods, Job Relations, and
  • Program Development, each enhancing workforce capability and productivity.
questions.final_answer: Ans: The four primary TWI programs are Job Instruction, Job Methods, Job Relations, and

questions.question: What are the key components of training documentation and record- / keeping?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Key components include training plans, attendance records, evaluation results
  • certifications, feedback, trainer details, objectives, schedules, and completion status tracking.
  • Short Essay

questions.question: Why is subject knowledge important for a trainer?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Subject knowledge is essential for a trainer because it builds credibility, ensures accurate
  • information delivery, boosts learner confidence, and enables effective question handling. It also
  • helps in designing relevant content and adapting training methods to meet learner needs
  • effectively.

questions.question: What are the four stages of the CIRO approach?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The four stages of the CIRO approach are Context, Input, Reaction, and Outcome. It
  • evaluates training by analyzing organizational needs , training design (Input)
  • participant feedback (Reaction), and the resulting behavioral and performance changes or
  • outcomes in the workplace.

questions.question: How does analyzing data from multiple sources improve training / evaluation?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Analyzing data from multiple sources improves training evaluation by providing a
  • well-rounded view of effectiveness, identifying gaps, validating outcomes, and ensuring
  • objectivity. It helps tailor future training, enhances decision-making, and aligns programs more
  • closely with organizational goals and learner needs.
questions.final_answer: closely with organizational goals and learner needs

questions.question: Why is training typically shorter in duration than development?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Training is typically shorter because it focuses on specific skills or tasks needed
  • immediately for a job. Development, however, is broader and long-term, aimed at overall
  • growth, leadership, and future roles, requiring more time and continuous learning efforts.
questions.final_answer: growth, leadership, and future roles, requiring more time and continuous learning efforts

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the training and development phase?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The primary objective of the training and development phase is to enhance employee
  • skills, knowledge, and competencies to improve performance, productivity, and job satisfaction.
  • It aims to align individual capabilities with organizational goals, preparing employees for current
  • roles and future career growth.
